questions.question_text: In a theatrical play, what is the script primarily used for?
options: B) Providing the spoken dialogues for actors
questions.answer: B) Providing the spoken dialogues for actors

What does a 'puppet' represent in traditional storytelling theatre?
options: C) A movable figure controlled by a person to act out characters
questions.answer: C) A movable figure controlled by a person to act out characters

questions.question_text: In the context of 'My Body in Motion', what is 'choreography'?
options: C) The sequence of steps and movements in dance
questions.answer: C) The sequence of steps and movements in dance

options: A) By using only one type of paint
B) By combining visual art, music, dance, and technology in one performance

sections.section_name: Section B - Theory Short Answer Concepts

questions.question_text: Explain how facial expressions help in 'Unveiling Emotions' during a dramatic performance. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Facial expressions visibly convey the internal feelings of the character to the audience without words, making the performance highly emotional and realistic.

questions.question_text: What is the main difference between a shadow puppet show and a traditional stage play? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A shadow puppet show uses flat cutout figures casting silhouettes onto a lit screen, whereas a stage play features real human actors performing live.

questions.question_text: How does 'Harmony in Motion' contribute to a successful group dance performance? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Harmony ensures that all dancers move synchronously with the rhythm and each other, creating a visually unified and beautiful group presentation.

questions.question_text: Describe the role of a 'director' in a theatre company. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The director guides the actors, oversees the staging, and coordinates all creative aspects to bring the script's vision to life successfully.

questions.question_text: Why is the integration of visual arts (like set design) and performing arts important for 'The Grand Finale'? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Combining stunning visual sets with dynamic performances creates a powerful, immersive experience that captivates the audience during the grand finale.

sections.section_name: Section C - Practical Tasks: Composition & Observation

questions.question_text: Design a stage set layout on paper for a school play titled 'The Magical Forest'. Include a backdrop, two side trees, and a central acting space. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: Assess the spatial layout and depth perspective on the paper. The backdrop must show a layered forest scene. The side trees should frame the central acting space effectively. Points awarded for creative use of proportion, clear focal points, and neat line work outlining the stage dimensions.

questions.question_text: Sketch three distinct facial masks representing 'Joy', 'Anger', and 'Sorrow' to be used in a theatrical performance. Apply shading to highlight facial contours. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: Evaluate the accuracy of the emotional expressions through exaggerated eyebrows, mouth shapes, and eye positioning. Smooth pencil shading should define the 3D form of the masks. High marks are given for distinct differentiation between the three emotions and clear anatomical structuring.

sections.section_name: Section D - Practical Tasks: Applied Design & Messaging

questions.question_text: Create a vibrant promotional poster for your school's upcoming Dance and Drama Festival. Include a catchy title, date, and illustrations merging dance and theatre elements. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: The poster must have strong visual impact using bold lettering for the title. The layout should balance text with illustrations, such as a dancer leaping next to tragedy/comedy theatre masks. Points awarded for vibrant color application, clear typography for the date/venue, and overall creative integration of the two themes.

questions.question_text: Design a storyboard sequence consisting of four panels that narrates a short mime act about 'Finding a Lost Key'. Use clear stick figures and action lines. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Evaluation Criteria: The panels must show a clear, logical sequence of actions: searching, finding, reacting, and resolving. The stick figures must display strong body language and gestures indicating a mime performance. High scores for the effective use of action lines, facial expressions within the minimalist figures, and a coherent visual narrative.
